title: Local ComfyUI / ControlNet Feasibility Bake-off

shared_parameters.rgb_source: output/phase0c/rgb/front.png (Blender perspective cubemap front face, 1024x1024 → resized 512x512)

depth_input.convention_in_png: near=BLACK, far=WHITE (standard Z-distance mapping; small distance → 0, large distance → 255)
depth_input.controlnet_expected_convention: near=WHITE, far=BLACK (MiDaS inverse-depth convention used in control_v11f1p_sd15_depth training)
depth_input.convention_mismatch_note: The depth PNG has INVERTED depth relative to ControlNet's training convention. Near objects (sofa foreground) mapped to 0 (black); ControlNet expected them at 255 (white). This means Test B ran with depth conditioning that told the model 'sofa is far, back wall is near' — opposite of reality.

wall_geometry.note: Back wall topology not preserved. Input has column at right-center and TV unit wall; output shows plain textured grey wall spanning full width.

openings.note: Left-side open archway to kitchen (visible in input) is absent. Model replaced that region with decorative plants.

ceiling.note: Flat white ceiling preserved at similar height. Recessed spotlights not reproduced.

cabinetry.note: Floating TV shelf unit absent. Output shows fireplace-style TV embedded in wall instead.

furniture_position.note: Sectional sofa is present but relocated and reshaped. Layout shifted vs. input.

furniture_count.note: Sofa, coffee table, and TV present. But right-side credenza/sideboard missing; added ottoman not in source.

major_proportions.note: Room scale and camera height roughly similar. Width and depth of space broadly comparable.

camera_composition.note: Perspective angle and field of view approximately match. Camera appears slightly more elevated in output.

material_intent.note: Input: uniform light grey. Output: warm taupe/beige palette with concrete-textured walls. Significant colour departure.

hallucinated_objects.note: Dry grass/pampas plant added. Fireplace not in source. Candle on coffee table not in source.

missing_objects.note: Kitchen opening missing. Floating TV shelves missing. Framed artwork missing. Structural column absent.

test_A.summary: Test A produces a photorealistic, coherent interior but diverges significantly from the source. Denoise=0.65 allows the diffusion model to rebuild large portions of the image, losing structural geometry, openings, and material accuracy. No ControlNet conditioning means the model relies only on the (down-sampled, noisy) latent from the Blender render, which is insufficient to constrain layout at this denoising strength.

wall_geometry.note: Output zooms into back wall/TV unit area due to depth inversion — ControlNet interpreted far=white as near=white, pulling back wall forward. Flanking walls absent.

openings.note: No door or opening to kitchen visible. Depth inversion amplified back wall and suppressed side openings.

ceiling.note: Ceiling partially visible at top of frame with pendant-style lights not in source.

cabinetry.note: TV unit with a horizontal wood shelf element is vaguely present (matches source concept) but the surrounding cabinet panels flanking it are not in source. Overall wall treatment is wrong.

furniture_position.note: Sofa barely visible at bottom of frame. Furniture pushed to extreme foreground edge due to scale distortion.

furniture_count.note: Only partial sofa visible. Coffee table, sideboard, plants all absent.

major_proportions.note: Room appears extremely compressed — output shows tight close-up of back wall rather than room interior. Wrong scale entirely.

camera_composition.note: Composition does not match source. Depth inversion caused model to treat back wall as near plane, collapsing room depth. Completely wrong framing.

material_intent.note: Neutral white/light grey palette closer to source intent than Test A. Wood shelf element matches warm-wood accent in source.

hallucinated_objects.note: Fewer hallucinated decorative objects than Test A. Added white cabinet panels and pendant lights not in source but fewer pure inventions.

missing_objects.note: Room opening, sofa, coffee table, column, artwork, full back wall all missing or misrepresented.

test_B.summary: Test B produced a structurally distorted result. The primary cause is depth convention mismatch: our depth PNG encodes near=black (standard Z-distance), but control_v11f1p_sd15_depth was trained on MiDaS inverse-depth maps where near=white. The ControlNet therefore received inverted depth, commanding the model to treat the far back wall as the closest surface. This collapsed room depth and zoomed into the back wall. Test B does not constitute a valid evaluation of ControlNet Depth conditioning.

depth_verdict_rationale: Under current conditions, adding ControlNet Depth conditioning produced worse output than RGB-only on 7 of 11 criteria (proportions, camera composition, furniture position, furniture count, openings, missing objects, wall geometry). However this result is confounded by a depth convention inversion bug: the depth PNG was produced with near=black, but control_v11f1p_sd15_depth expects near=white (MiDaS convention). Test B is therefore NOT a valid bake-off result — it is a measurement of 'inverted depth conditioning'. The verdict DEPTH_HURTS_QUALITY applies to the current implementation, not to ControlNet Depth in principle.
vram_verdict_rationale: RTX 2060 6GB successfully ran both tests with ComfyUI --lowvram --cpu-vae at 512x512. Phase 0H failure was a tooling issue (naive diffusers pipeline), not a hardware barrier. ComfyUI sequential offloading resolves the memory constraint. Test A: ~7.6 it/s. Test B: ~5.5 it/s. Both well within budget.

root_causes.title: Depth convention inversion
root_causes.description: output/phase0i/input/depth.png encodes near=black (Z-distance: small distance → 0). control_v11f1p_sd15_depth is trained on MiDaS inverse-depth where near=white. Fix: invert the depth PNG (pixel = 255 - current_pixel) before passing to ControlNet.

root_causes.title: Denoise too high for structure preservation
root_causes.description: denoise=0.65 allows the model to rebuild 65% of the image from noise, losing source structure. Even Test A (no ControlNet) could not preserve wall topology, openings, or cabinetry at this strength. Lower denoise (0.3–0.45) or a stronger ControlNet signal is required for layout fidelity.

recommended_next_actions: Fix depth inversion: apply pixel = 255 - current_pixel to depth.png before ControlNet use
Lower denoise to 0.40 for stronger input image constraint
Re-run bake-off with corrected depth to obtain a valid DEPTH_CLEARLY_HELPS / DEPTH_SLIGHTLY_HELPS / NO_MEANINGFUL_DIFFERENCE measurement
Do NOT proceed to Phase 0J until corrected bake-off is complete

definition_of_done_status.depth_verdict: DONE — DEPTH_HURTS_QUALITY (depth inversion bug confounds result)
